option_description: Whether stored passwords are held under a one-way KDF (hashed) rather than in plaintext or under a reversible cipher.
security_impact: Drives "Plaintext or reversibly-encrypted password storage" — when false (passwords stored cleartext or reversibly encrypted) that exposure fires, yielding instant mass account takeover on disclosure of the store. Also an OR-condition of "Weak / unsalted / fast password hashes".

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the leading bytes of stored password hashes from the credential store to confirm an adaptive-KDF prefix rather than a raw digest or recoverable value.
how_to_obtain.command: SELECT substring(password_hash for 12) FROM users LIMIT 5;
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each stored hash begins with an adaptive-KDF identifier — '$argon2id$' (secure, preferred), '$scrypt$', '$2a$'/'$2b$'/'$2y$' (bcrypt), or 'pbkdf2_sha256$' (Django-style). A 32-hex (MD5), 40-hex (SHA-1), or 64-hex (raw SHA-256) value with no algorithm prefix, or a value that decrypts back to the password, is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the source/config of the password-handling path to confirm no cleartext storage and no reversible cipher is applied to passwords.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Source/config review confirms the hashing call uses Argon2id (m>=19 MiB, t>=2, p=1) or an approved equivalent; no code path stores or logs the cleartext password and no reversible cipher is applied to passwords.

option_description: Whether the password KDF is a memory-hard adaptive function (Argon2id preferred; scrypt/bcrypt/PBKDF2 acceptable) rather than a fast digest like MD5/SHA-1/raw SHA-256.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak / unsalted / fast password hashes" — when false (a fast/unsalted digest is used) that exposure fires, permitting rapid offline GPU/rainbow-table cracking of the entire credential dump.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the stored-hash prefix to identify the KDF family in use.
how_to_obtain.command: SELECT substring(password_hash for 12) FROM users LIMIT 5;
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each stored hash begins with an adaptive-KDF identifier — '$argon2id$' (secure, preferred), '$scrypt$', '$2a$'/'$2b$'/'$2y$' (bcrypt), or 'pbkdf2_sha256$' (Django-style). A 32-hex (MD5), 40-hex (SHA-1), or 64-hex (raw SHA-256) value with no algorithm prefix, or a value that decrypts back to the password, is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm in source/config review that the hashing call uses an approved memory-hard adaptive KDF.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Source/config review confirms the hashing call uses Argon2id (m>=19 MiB, t>=2, p=1) or an approved equivalent; no code path stores or logs the cleartext password and no reversible cipher is applied to passwords.

option_description: Whether each stored password has a unique, sufficiently long salt so identical passwords produce different hashes and precomputed (rainbow) tables are defeated.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak / unsalted / fast password hashes" — when false (no salt, a shared/global salt, or salt < 32 bits) that exposure fires, enabling rainbow-table and bulk offline cracking.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Self-join the credential table on equal hashes for distinct users to detect missing or shared salt.
how_to_obtain.command: SELECT password_hash FROM users u1 JOIN users u2 ON u1.password_hash = u2.password_hash AND u1.id <> u2.id;
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Two accounts that set the same chosen password yield DIFFERENT stored hashes (proves per-credential salt); the join above should return NO rows for distinct users. Identical hashes for identical passwords indicate missing/shared salt — INSECURE.

option_description: Whether the KDF cost parameters meet the OWASP minimum (Argon2id m>=19 MiB/t>=2/p=1; bcrypt cost>=10; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256>=600k) so the hash resists offline GPU/ASIC cracking.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak / unsalted / fast password hashes" — when false (cost tuned for speed / below the minimum profile) that exposure fires, dropping the cost of offline cracking the credential dump.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the application password-hashing config for Argon2id cost parameters.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: memory_cost >= 19456 KiB, time_cost (iterations) >= 2, parallelism = 1. Lower memory_cost is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If bcrypt is in use, extract the cost field from a stored $2b$ hash.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The cost field (the number between the 2nd and 3rd '$' in a $2b$ hash) is >= 10. A cost of 04-09 is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If PBKDF2 is in use (e.g. for FIPS), grep the config for the iteration count and PRF.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: iterations >= 600000 with HMAC-SHA-256 (OWASP target). NIST SP 800-63B sets a floor of at least 10,000 'as large as server performance will allow'.

option_description: Whether API keys, SSH/private keys, and other long-lived machine credentials are held in a dedicated secret manager/vault and injected at runtime.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Hardcoded / unvaulted API, SSH and private keys" — when false (keys not vaulted) that exposure fires, exposing long-lived keys to harvest from repos/artifacts for direct impersonation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan source and git history for embedded key material and API keys (a secret-scanner run should be clean).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches in source/history. A secret-scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog) run is clean. Any hardcoded API key or private key block is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm with the team that machine credentials are sourced from a secret manager/KMS-backed store and injected at runtime rather than baked into images or config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Keys are vaulted in a secret manager (e.g. Vault / cloud KMS-backed store) and injected at runtime; no hardcoded source, image-embedded, or committed-config secrets exist.

option_description: Whether secrets (API/SSH/private keys, passwords) are hardcoded in source, baked into container images, or committed in plaintext config / IaC / .env to version control.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Hardcoded / unvaulted API, SSH and private keys" — when true (secrets committed to config/IaC) that exposure fires; the hardcoded secrets are harvested from repos/artifacts and replayed for impersonation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan source, config, IaC, and git history for embedded key/secret material.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches in source/history. A secret-scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog) run is clean. Any hardcoded API key or private key block is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether credentials are submitted and verified only over TLS — the login page and all authenticated endpoints are exclusively HTTPS, with no cleartext credential acceptance.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Credentials transmitted in cleartext" — when false (credentials accepted over HTTP / a login form posting to an http:// action) that exposure fires, letting a network attacker sniff/MITM and replay the credential.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request the login endpoint over plain HTTP and check for an HTTPS redirect and an https:// form action.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP is redirected (301/308) to HTTPS and the login form action is an https:// URL; an HSTS header is present on authenticated responses. A login form served or posting over http:// is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether HTTP Strict Transport Security is set on authenticated responses so browsers refuse to submit credentials over cleartext HTTP after first contact.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Credentials transmitted in cleartext" — when false (no HSTS) a downgrade/strip attack can coerce the client onto HTTP, contributing to that exposure firing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the response headers from the login / authenticated endpoints for a Strict-Transport-Security header (and confirm the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP is redirected (301/308) to HTTPS and the login form action is an https:// URL; an HSTS header is present on authenticated responses. A login form served or posting over http:// is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether repeated failed authentication on an account is throttled or locked out (e.g. exponential backoff bound to the account, not just source IP) to blunt online brute force.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Online brute force and credential stuffing" — when false (unlimited failed attempts with no delay or lockout) that exposure fires, letting attackers recover weak passwords by unbounded guessing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit a burst of failed logins against one account and watch for throttling/lockout responses.
how_to_obtain.command: for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -d "user=victim&pass=wrong$i" https://<host>/login; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: After a small number of failures, responses change to throttled/locked (e.g. 429, escalating delay, or lockout message); consecutive failures never exceed 100. Constant 200/401 with no delay across many attempts is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether new/changed passwords are screened against known-breached and common-password corpuses (e.g. Pwned Passwords via the k-anonymity range API) and rejected if compromised.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Online brute force and credential stuffing" — when false (no breach screening; previously-breached passwords accepted) that exposure fires, since reused breached passwords are replayed at scale and succeed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run the Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range flow for a known-breached password and confirm the registration/change flow rejects it.
how_to_obtain.command: P=$(printf 'Password1' | openssl sha1 | tr a-f A-F | cut -d' ' -f2); curl -s https://api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/${P:0:5} | grep -i ${P:5}
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The k-anonymity flow (send first 5 SHA-1 hex chars to /range/{prefix}, match the 35-char suffix in the response with its breach count) is what the app must run at password-set time and REJECT non-zero matches. Confirm the registration/change flow rejects a known-breached password like 'Password1'.
how_to_obtain.source: Have I Been Pwned — Pwned Passwords Range API (k-anonymity)

option_description: Whether a second authentication factor is available/enforced so that credential theft alone does not grant access.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Online brute force and credential stuffing" — when false (password-only, no second factor) that exposure fires; OWASP cites MFA as stopping ~99.9% of account compromises, so its absence is the dominant credential-stuffing gap.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify MFA is offered and enforced for sensitive/privileged access by reviewing the authentication design and policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MFA (TOTP/WebAuthn/possession factor) is offered and enforced where appropriate; OWASP cites MFA would stop ~99.9% of account compromises. Password-only with no MFA option for privileged accounts is a gap.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Credential Stuffing Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: The configured cap on consecutive failed authentication attempts before lockout/throttling; NIST SP 800-63B requires this be <= 100.
security_impact: Feeds "Online brute force and credential stuffing" — a cap above 100 (or effectively unbounded) is an OR-condition for that exposure, widening the online-guessing window against accounts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Drive failed logins against one account and observe the attempt number at which throttle/lockout engages.
how_to_obtain.command: for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -d "user=victim&pass=wrong$i" https://<host>/login; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: After a small number of failures, responses change to throttled/locked (e.g. 429, escalating delay, or lockout message); consecutive failures never exceed 100. Constant 200/401 with no delay across many attempts is INSECURE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the configured lockout/throttle threshold value against the NIST <=100 consecutive-failures ceiling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The configured consecutive-failure threshold is at or below 100 (NIST SP 800-63B caps consecutive failed attempts at <=100); a threshold above 100 or 'no limit' is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether failed-login responses are identical (a single generic message) regardless of cause, so the credential store does not leak which usernames exist.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Username enumeration via differential responses" — when false (distinct 'no such user' vs 'wrong password' messages) that exposure fires, letting attackers build a valid-username target list for brute force / stuffing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit a login for a non-existent user and one for a real user with a wrong password, then compare the responses.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Both requests return the SAME message and comparable timing. A 'no such user' vs 'wrong password' distinction (or measurable timing difference) is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether the login path takes comparable time for valid and invalid usernames (e.g. always running a dummy hash verification) so timing does not betray account existence.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Username enumeration via differential responses" — when false (measurable timing difference between valid and invalid usernames) that exposure fires, enabling timing-based enumeration even when error text is generic.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Time the login response for a non-existent user versus a real user with a wrong password and compare latency.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Both requests return the SAME message and comparable timing. A 'no such user' vs 'wrong password' distinction (or measurable timing difference) is INSECURE.

option_description: The minimum allowed password length; NIST/OWASP recommend >=8 with MFA, >=15 without MFA.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak credential-strength policy" — when the minimum is too low (below 8, or below 15 with no MFA) that exposure fires, leaving accounts vulnerable to guessing/cracking.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the password policy/config for the enforced minimum length and the broader length/composition rules.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy/config shows min length >= 8 (>=15 without MFA), max >= 64, paste allowed, no composition mandates, and no scheduled expiry. NIST: 'Verifiers SHOULD NOT require memorized secrets to be changed arbitrarily (e.g., periodically).'

option_description: Whether the policy caps maximum password length below 64 characters (which blocks long passphrases and is a NIST/OWASP anti-pattern).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak credential-strength policy" — when true (max length capped below 64) that exposure fires, since a low cap weakens passphrase strength and often hints at storage that truncates or fails to hash properly.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the password policy/config for any maximum-length cap and confirm it permits at least 64 characters.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy/config shows min length >= 8 (>=15 without MFA), max >= 64, paste allowed, no composition mandates, and no scheduled expiry. NIST: 'Verifiers SHOULD NOT require memorized secrets to be changed arbitrarily (e.g., periodically).'

option_description: Whether the policy imposes character-composition mandates or arbitrary periodic password expiry — both NIST anti-patterns that push users toward predictable patterns.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Weak credential-strength policy" — when true (composition rules or scheduled forced rotation) that exposure fires, as NIST states verifiers SHOULD NOT impose composition rules or require periodic rotation absent evidence of compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the password policy/config for character-composition mandates and any scheduled/periodic expiry.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy/config shows min length >= 8 (>=15 without MFA), max >= 64, paste allowed, no composition mandates, and no scheduled expiry. NIST: 'Verifiers SHOULD NOT require memorized secrets to be changed arbitrarily (e.g., periodically).'

option_description: Whether API/SSH/machine keys have a defined periodic rotation lifecycle rather than being static long-lived secrets.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "No rotation or revocation on compromise" — when false (static, never-rotated keys) that exposure fires, extending an attacker's window indefinitely after a key is stolen.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm with operations that a documented key-rotation schedule and immediate-revoke capability exist for API/SSH keys.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm an operational runbook/control exists to revoke and reissue a leaked credential or key, and that password reset is forced on evidence of compromise (NIST: rotate only when 'there is evidence of compromise'). API/SSH keys have a rotation schedule and immediate-revoke capability.

option_description: Whether a documented path exists to force password reset / revoke and reissue a credential or key promptly on evidence of compromise.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "No rotation or revocation on compromise" — when false (no revocation path, no forced reset on breach) that exposure fires, leaving a stolen credential usable after a known compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify an operational runbook/control covers revoke-and-reissue of a leaked credential or key and forced password reset on compromise.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm an operational runbook/control exists to revoke and reissue a leaked credential or key, and that password reset is forced on evidence of compromise (NIST: rotate only when 'there is evidence of compromise'). API/SSH keys have a rotation schedule and immediate-revoke capability.

option_description: Whether passwords, API keys, and private keys are redacted and never written to application logs, error traces, or telemetry.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Credentials leaked to logs or URLs" — when false (credentials written to logs/traces) that exposure fires, creating a secondary harvestable copy of the secret outside the protected store.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep application and access logs for password/key values and Authorization headers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches. Any logged password value, API key, private-key block, or Basic-auth credential — or a credential present in an access-log URL query string — is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether credentials ever appear in request URLs or query strings (where they land in access logs, browser history, and referrers).
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Credentials leaked to logs or URLs" — when true (credentials placed in URL/query) that exposure fires, since the secret is captured in access logs and proxies as a harvestable copy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep access logs for credential values in URL query strings (and check the app's request patterns).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches. Any logged password value, API key, private-key block, or Basic-auth credential — or a credential present in an access-log URL query string — is INSECURE.

option_description: Whether read access to the credential/hash table and the secret store is restricted to the minimum set of principals (only the auth service identity), so ordinary app roles cannot dump hashes or the pepper.
security_impact: An OR-trigger of "Over-broad access to the credential store" — when false (broad read access across roles/services) that exposure fires, multiplying the principals who could exfiltrate the hash column or secret store.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate grants on the credential table (and the secret store) to confirm only the auth service principal can read the hash column.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only the authentication service principal can read the password-hash column and the pepper/secret store; broad SELECT or shared service accounts with read access are INSECURE. (PostgreSQL \dp; use SHOW GRANTS on other engines.)

option_description: Whether an optional server-side secret (pepper) is applied in addition to the per-credential salt and held in a separate secret store/HSM, so a database-only leak does not enable cracking.
security_impact: Strengthens resistance under "Weak / unsalted / fast password hashes" and "Over-broad access to the credential store" — when false (no pepper, or pepper stored alongside the hashes) a DB-only leak suffices to crack hashes, an OR-condition contributing to those exposures.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm via design review that a secret-salt/pepper is applied and sourced from a secret store separate from the password database.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Design review confirms a secret-salt/pepper of >= 112-bit security strength is applied via an additional KDF/HMAC step and is sourced from a secret store separate from the password database (NIST: 'salt value that is secret and known only to the verifier').
